\paragraph{What we find.} First, how fragile a conclusion is follows from its separation and the sample size: real datasets of all four designs lie within the margin of the same-graph reference in nearly every case, the exceptions being a few rows with too few pairs and a small offset of the method that shows in Arena outcome flips (Section~\ref{sec:headline}). Second, noise and an adversary differ by orders of magnitude: random alterations of the size of the smallest targeted change essentially never reverse a conclusion, while a pair that the published intervals separate loses its separation under a targeted change of a few tenths of a percent to about one percent of the votes in the large crowd and judge datasets (Section~\ref{sec:survival}). Third, the comparison with the reference has limited power: in a simulated control it did not respond to the departures tried, so close agreement is not evidence that Bradley--Terry fits, and the one design effect we find is in the published interval, about \seRatioExpert{} times the model-based one for MT-Bench expert labels (Section~\ref{sec:design}, Appendix~\ref{app:control}). We add a regression that predicts $k^{*}$ from separation, size, density and ties, no better than the dataset's own simulation and worse for held-out designs (Section~\ref{sec:rule}), and checks that one-shot influence ranking, the usual approximation, finds the smallest change in only part of the conclusions (Section~\ref{sec:search}).

The same-graph comparison asks whether a dataset is more or less fragile than its own statistics imply; whether the \emph{labeller} matters is a question about two labellings of identical items. Figure~\ref{fig:design} shows $\Delta$ for every dataset by design (A) and the paired difference of $\Delta$ between each LLM judge and the crowd on the identical Arena battles (B; \matchedBoot{} joint resamples of battles, \matchedPairs{} $z$-stratified pairs per member and family). All \nPairedEquiv{} of the \nPairedRows{} paired differences of the \nMatchedJudges{} judge contrasts are equivalent within the margin; \nPairedExZero{} of them exclude zero, none with a point difference above \pairedExZeroAbsMax{} on the log scale (interval ends reach \pairedExZeroEndMax{}). On MT-Bench, experts against GPT-4 on the identical questions, with only \mtMatchedPairs{} pairs in range, outcome flips are equivalent ($\mtPairedFlip$ [$\mtPairedFlipLo$, $\mtPairedFlipHi$]) and deletion is undecided ($\mtPairedDel$ [$\mtPairedDelLo$, $\mtPairedDelHi$]). We find no design-specific departure beyond $\pm\deltaMargin$, but $\Delta$ is not a test of misfit: on data simulated from the MT-Bench human graph with a departure added (overdispersion up to a design effect of \ctlDesEffMax{}, position bias, a cyclic or a pair-specific component), $\Delta$ stayed within the margin at every size tried, the largest $|\Delta|$ being \ctlDeltaMax{} (Appendix~\ref{app:control}). The sizes were fixed in advance, not matched to real departures, and none reached the margin. A departure of the interval rather than of the count does appear: the median ratio of the cluster-bootstrap to the model-based standard error of a gap is \seRatioExpert{} for MT-Bench expert labels (design effect \seDesEffExpert{} from the questions), against \seNullExpert{} for the same-graph simulation of that dataset. The ratio is \seRatioCrowd{} for Arena crowd votes against \seNullCrowd{} in simulation, an effect of ties, and \seRatioJudge{} and \seRatioSports{} for the LLM judges and the NBA seasons, as in simulation.

shown.message:
I fixed the design claim that `story-repo` flagged in `paper-repo`#14, and the fix is waiting in PR #15 (`candidate-v3` into `main`).

- **Abstract:** it no longer says fragility follows from separation and sample size, "not from the evaluation design". It now says real data stay within the margin of the same-graph reference, which a first-order identity makes largely expected. The design shows instead in how wide the bootstrap interval is relative to its model-based width. The abstract has no numbers and is 226 words.
- **Introduction and Section 4.3:** the first finding and the last sentences of 4.3 say the same thing. The Discussion already had the right wording, so I left it alone.
- **Checks:** in a scratch build the main text still ends on page 9, and there are no Type 3 fonts, no overfull boxes and no undefined references. I haven't looked at the system's build of `dev`.
- **Issue #14:** I closed it with a comment pointing to PR #15.
- **Next:** I'll merge PR #15 into `main` once it has the reviews it needs. That moves the head of the release PR #11 again, so `internal-review-repo` will have to review it again.
